tools.name: analyze_job
tools.desc: Score a job description against the resume and write proposals
tools.summary: Deterministic match: synonym groups, stemming, TF-IDF cosine at 0.15. Writes variants/<v>/proposals.json with resume_key, evidence, score and a null suggested_change, plus the gaps that must not be invented.
tools.when_to_use: You have a job description and want to know which existing resume lines already answer it.
tools.when_not_to_use: You want prose rewritten, or a model's opinion. This reads phrases, not intent.
tools.example: PYANY_VARIANT=acme PYANY_JD='We need Golang and observability' doit analyze_job

tools.name: apply_approved
tools.desc: Fold approved proposals into the variant resume
tools.summary: Writes variants/<v>/resume.json from variants/<v>/approved.json and nothing else. Without approved.json it fails before touching the filesystem, which is the gate that stops an unreviewed edit.
tools.when_to_use: After a human has approved proposals and filled in suggested_change.
tools.when_not_to_use: Before approval, or to force an edit through. There is no override flag on purpose.
preconditions: variants/<v>/approved.json exists with at least one item

tools.name: build_pdf
tools.desc: Render the variant resume to a validated PDF with pdfcpu
tools.summary: resume.json to pdfcpu JSON to create, validate, optimize. Writes variants/<v>/build/resume.pdf and status.json; fails on a validate error rather than serving a broken file.
tools.when_to_use: After apply_approved, when you need the PDF to preview or download.
tools.when_not_to_use: To check analysis results, or before the resume has any approved content.
preconditions: variants/<v>/resume.json exists, or the base resume does

tools.name: show_tasks
tools.desc: Print the five catalogue commands Needle can route
tools.summary: Reads the generated tools.json and prints name, scope and a runnable example. This is the task a router calls to discover what exists.
tools.when_to_use: You forgot the exact command name, or you are checking that a name is in the catalogue.
tools.when_not_to_use: To run a task. It only prints.

tools.name: start_dev
tools.desc: Start the local Flask dev server in the background
tools.summary: Spawns main.py serve on PYANY_PORT (default 5001) and writes its pid. Refuses on PythonAnywhere, where a second server would only burn the CPU quota.
tools.when_to_use: Working locally and you want the editor reachable on a port.
tools.when_not_to_use: On the PythonAnywhere host, or anywhere the site is already served.
